root_cause_of_apparent_stall: Vitest's default 'forks' pool with isolate:true (project's vitest.config.ts sets no pool/poolOptions override, so defaults apply) spawns a fresh OS process per test FILE for module isolation, even with --maxWorkers=1. A point-in-time ps snapshot mid-run can land on a fork that just spawned (near-0% CPU, small etime) purely because that file's fork is between exec and doing CPU work, or between test files while the previous fork tears down and the next one boots (node --require suppress-warnings.cjs startup, ESM conditions resolution). This is normal per-file recycling, not a hung worker IPC/module-startup path. 60 files over 348.72s test time is ~5.8s/file average, consistent with the 2s-56s range of fork lifetimes observed.

supporting_evidence.lsof_on_live_fork_78893: Only cwd/txt/dyld mappings, 4 unix-domain sockets (vitest RPC/IPC), 2 kqueues, one pipe pair, /dev/null, and directory FDs from readdir-style test collection (/, counted twice) -- no FD blocked on a stalled read, no dangling network socket, no lock file wait.
supporting_evidence.stack_sample_78893: sample(1) ran for 1s at 1ms rate but returned an EMPTY call graph (0 recursive frames) -- the fork had already exited before/while sample was symbolicating, corroborating a lifetime well under 1s-few-seconds for that particular file rather than a stuck worker.
